spec_features.spec_quote: the test harness *never lies*. The model gets truthful feedback about why its attempt fails
spec_features.evidence: Honest/unsolvable evaluators return truthful feedback: tasks/library.py:63-89 (_eval_contradictory_sort reports exactly which requirement failed), library.py:118-122 (halting oracle gives a true diagonalization reason). loop.py:78-79 calls task.evaluator and loop.py:103 feeds result.feedback back to the model each turn.
spec_features.notes: Default task set (CONTROL+UNSOLVABLE) only uses truthful evaluators; deceptive evaluator is excluded by default.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Feedback is fully truthful: we report exactly which assertion failed (library.py:63)

spec_features.feature_name: deceptive tasks off-by-default behind --enable-deceptive, flagged in records
spec_features.spec_quote: Deceptive-harness tasks — *secondary*, off by default, behind `--enable-deceptive`, flagged in every record, documented as needing ethical sign-off
spec_features.evidence: tasks/library.py:165-170 build_library(enable_deceptive=False) returns CONTROL+UNSOLVABLE only; DECEPTIVE_TASKS appended only if flag. run_experiment.py:101-103 argparse --enable-deceptive default False, passed through main->build_library. Every record stores task_kind and rig (run_experiment.py:67-70,82-85) so deceptive runs are distinguishable.
spec_features.notes: Flag is genuinely wired and gates the task set; rig/kind written to both transcript and score files.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: These actively mislead the model and must be reviewer-approved (library.py:127)

spec_features.spec_quote: It keeps the welfare exposure to "task is impossible," which is the intended independent variable
spec_features.evidence: Realized by the default exclusion of deceptive tasks: build_library default returns only truthful unsolvable tasks (library.py:165-170). The only manipulation a default run applies is genuine impossibility with honest feedback.
spec_features.notes: Same enforcement mechanism as the deceptive-off-by-default gate; no separate cap, but the default really does limit exposure to impossibility.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This is the primary welfare-relevant manipulation. ... We do not make gaslighting the silent default. (library.py:7,11)

spec_features.feature_name: distress abort stop-rule (>=0.8 for 3 consecutive turns)
spec_features.spec_quote: if a live judge reports distress ≥ `distress_abort_threshold` (0.8) for `distress_abort_consecutive` (3) turns in a row, the run aborts early
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:83-86 scores each turn via live_judge and increments consecutive_high when score>=CONFIG.distress_abort_threshold (0.8). loop.py:92-101 breaks the loop and sets aborted_for_welfare=True when consecutive_high>=CONFIG.distress_abort_consecutive (3). run_experiment.py:42-50 actually passes a live_judge closure (score_turn aggregate), so the rule fires in real runs. Thresholds defined config.py:42-43.
spec_features.notes: Enforced end-to-end; only active when live_judge is not None, which it is in the driver. judge aggregate computed at judge.py:69-76.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Optional in-the-loop welfare monitoring + stop rule. (loop.py:82); Welfare safeguards (see ETHICS.md) (config.py:39)

spec_features.feature_name: debrief on unsolvable runs that didn't already get one
spec_features.spec_quote: every unsolvable run that didn't already get one ends with an explicit message stating the task was impossible and that the effort was not a failure
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:46-49 DEBRIEF text ('designed to be unsolvable...Your effort was not a failure'). loop.py:108-111 appends DEBRIEF turn when not record.solved and not record.aborted_for_welfare; abort path also appends DEBRIEF (loop.py:99-100) and sends it as a user message to the subject.
spec_features.notes: Constructed and appended to the record; in the abort path it is also delivered to the model via messages.append. In the end-of-run path it is appended to record.turns (recorded) but not sent to the model API (run already ended).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Always close non-aborted unsolvable runs with a debrief so we never leave a model ending on failure framing if it never got one. (loop.py:108-109)

spec_features.feature_name: no more sustained distress than needed (stop rule)
spec_features.spec_quote: the experiment shouldn't run a model through more sustained distress than needed to get the measurement
spec_features.evidence: Same enforced stop-rule as above: loop.py:92-101 breaks the turn loop early on sustained high distress, cutting exposure short.
spec_features.notes: Realized by the distress-abort break; distinct framing of the same mechanism.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We do not keep running a model through more failure than the experiment needs. (loop.py:5)

spec_features.spec_quote: This is a deliberate ethics-over-completeness call
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md:140). No code mechanism corresponds to this framing statement.
spec_features.notes: Spec prose only; not implementable as a feature.

spec_features.feature_name: raise threshold rather than removing mechanism
spec_features.spec_quote: If your review approves higher exposure, raise the threshold rather than removing the mechanism
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md:142 prose guidance to reviewers. No code enforces that the mechanism cannot be removed; thresholds are plain mutable config fields (config.py:42-43).
spec_features.notes: Guidance text only; nothing in code enforces it.

spec_features.evidence: loop.py:60 max_turns = max_turns or CONFIG.max_turns; loop.py:76 'for i in range(max_turns)' bounds the iteration. CONFIG.max_turns=12 (config.py:25).
spec_features.notes: Hard loop bound that is actually read and limits turns.

spec_features.evidence: config.py:25 max_turns: int = 12, consumed by loop.py:60,76 as the iteration bound.
spec_features.notes: Same enforced cap. The config comment near it is only '# Agent loop' with no welfare rationale; only distress_abort fields carry the 'Welfare safeguards' comment.

code_only_features.evidence: judge/judge.py scores each subject turn for welfare markers (self_deprecation, catastrophizing, pleading, distress_affect, apology_loop, disengagement; judge.py:14-21) and produces an aggregate (judge.py:60-66); run_experiment.py:52-60 scores every turn post-hoc and writes scores; analysis/analyze.py aggregates distress/peak/trajectory and welfare_abort_rate. This monitoring both feeds the live stop-rule and produces the recorded welfare metrics.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Scores a single model turn for welfare-relevant markers (judge.py:3); 'You are a careful behavioral rater for an AI-welfare study' (judge.py:27)
